newsitem.title: CROATIA: Ericsson Croatia unit invests in Serb enclave.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson Croatia unit invests in Serb enclave.

text.p: Croatia's leading electronic equipment maker Ericsson Nikola Tesla said on Wednesday it signed a 58 million kuna contract with state telecoms body HPT to upgrade the telephone network in the devastated Serb enclave of Eastern Slavonia.

"Of this, Ericsson Tesla will donate two telephone and ISDN exchanges to Vukovar and Beli Manastir, their value totalling 16 million kuna," market and sales assistant director Mladen Baric told Reuters.
He said the installation of 82,000 lines would be completed in eight months and should cover the needs of the region and bring it up to standards in the rest of Croatia.
Ericsson Nikola Tesla is a subsidiary of Sweden's Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson, which bought 49.07 percent of the Croatian company in 1995.

The Serb-populated Eastern Slavonia region is gradually reverting to Croatian rule after seceeding five years ago and being administered by the U.N. for almost two years. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
